Coram:
Ms. Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua, Judge.
Whether approved for reporting?
For the petitioner : Mr. C.N. Singh with Mr. Shashi  Kiran Negi, Advocate.
For the respondents : Mr. L.N. Sharma, Additional  Advocate General.

Jyotsna Rewal Dua, Judge Petitioners seek direction to the respondents to acquire their land utilized for construction of Maryog-Lana- Kasar-Wasni Road and pay them compensation in accordance with law.

2. The facts projected by the petitioners are that:-
2(i).
The respondents have constructed Maryog-Lana Kasar-Wasni in the year 1988-89.

The land belonging to the petitioner comprised in Khata No.9 min/2 Khatauni No. 14 min/9, Khasra No.3, Khata No.6 min/2, Khatauni No.11 min/9,
Khasra No.6, Khata No.8 min/2, Khatauni No.13 min/9, Khasra No.38, Khata No.4 min/1, Khatauni No.4
Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes min/1 min, 2 min, 8, Khasra No.18, Khata No. 5 min/1, Khatauni No.5 min/1, Khasra No. 17, Khata No.4 min/1, Khatauni No.4 min/1 min, 2min, 8, Khasra No. 16, Khata No.4 min/1, Khatauni No. 4 min/1 min, 2min, 8, Khasra No.14, Khata No.8 min/2, Khatauni No. 13 min/9, Khasra No. 7 and Khata No.9 min/2, Khatauni No.14 min/9, Khasra No. 2, situated in Up Sampda Shakrora, Patwar Circle Drabli,
Hadbast No.333/1, Sub Tehsil Narag, District Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh,
(hereinafter referred to as the 'subject land') was utilized by respondent for construction of the aforesaid road.
However, no compensation was paid to the petitioners in lieu thereof.
Petitioners' aforesaid land was not acquired by the respondents in accordance with law.

Respondents have not initiated the acquisition proceedings qua above described land of the petitioners and have not paid any compensation, whereas, for the construction of the same road, the respondents had utilized several other parcels of land in villages Maryog, Baryudi,

sentences.text: The respondents had duly acquired the land of the villagers in aforesaid villages but left out the land of the petitioners in village Shakrora.

The Land Acquisition Collector had passed Award No.2 of 2019 dated 21.01.2019 for acquisition of lands in revenue villages Baryudi, Tehsil Pachhad,
District Sirmour (H.P.) utilized for the construction of Maryog-Kotla-Baryudi Road.
However, the petitioners have been discriminated.
Their land utilized for construction of the aforesaid road has not been acquired in accordance with law.
The petitioners have not been paid any compensation thereof.

3. Respondents in its reply have taken the stand that the land of the petitioners utilized for construction of the road was voluntarily surrendered by them/their predecessors-in-interest in favour of the respondents.
Hence, there arises no question of acquiring it or paying them compensation.

Plea of delay and laches on the part of the petitioners in instituting this writ petition has also been raised for opposing the prayer for initiating land acquisition proceedings for the subject land.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and considered the case file:-
4(i).
It is not in dispute that the respondents have constructed the road in question in the year 1988-89.
For the construction of the road, the respondents have utilized several parcels of land, including the land falling in Villages Maryog, Baryudi, Cheola Bhakang and Daron Devaria etc.
It has not been denied by the respondents that the subject land (owned by the petitioners) had been utilized by them for construction of the road.

4(ii) The plea that the petitioners/their predecessor-in- interest had voluntarily surrendered the subject land and had consented for the construction of the road in question, stands falsified from the fact that award No.2 of 2019 was passed on 21.01.2019 in relation to the acquisition of certain parcels of land for construction of this very road.
The aforesaid award covered the lands located in several villages.
The respondents have not placed on record any document from which the alleged consent of the petitioners or their predecessor-in-interest could be inferred.
4(iii).
It would also be appropriate to refer to the judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court on 28.06.2023 in CWP No.6581/2021 (Labdhu Ram Vs. State of H.P. & Ors).

sentences.text: The petitioner therein had raised a factual plea that though certain others, whose lands were utilized for the road, were paid the compensation, but he was denied the same even though his land was also utilized for construction of same road.
Road in that case was laid in the year 1995-96.

Taking note of various pronouncements, viz. (1986) 2 SCC 68 (State of Himachal Pradesh Vs Umeed Ram Sharma); (2016) 7 SCC 498 (Swaraj Abhiyan(I) vs. Union of India and ors.); (2020) 9 SCC 356 (Hari Krishna Mandir Trust vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors.); (2020) 4 SCC 572 (D.B. Basnett Vs.
Collector East District, Gangtok, Sikkim and Anr.); (2021) 14 SCC 703 (B.K. Ravichandra and Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors.); (2022) 7 SCC 508 (Sukh Dutt Ratra & Anr. Vs. sentences.text: 2 Pradesh & Ors.), the contention of delay and laches raised by the respondents- State was turned down.
The observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court that the State cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated, were reiterated.

It will be appropriate to extract following paragraphs from Labdhu Ram's case (supra):-
"18.
In Sukh Dutt Ratra, supra, the appellant's land had been utilized for construction of road in 1972-73 without initiating any proceedings for acquisition and without paying any compensation.

When the petitioner filed a writ petition on the basis of relief granted to other owners whose land was so acquired, the said Writ petition was dismissed by the High Court holding that there were disputed questions of law and fact for determination on the starting point of limitation, which cannot be adjudicated in the writ proceeding and the petitioners were given liberty to approach the Civil Court.

The Supreme Court reversed the said decision and held that nobody can be deprived of liberty or property without due process, or authorization of law and the State has a higher responsibility in demonstrating that it has acted within the confines of legality, and had not tarnished the basic principle of the rule of law.
It held that State, merely on the ground of delay and laches, cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated.

It observed that the State was initiating acquisition proceedings selectively and not in every case like that of the appellants whose land was taken, and at every stage it sought to shirk its responsibility of acquiring land required for public use in the manner prescribed by law.
It held that the State cannot shield itself behind the ground of delay and laches in such a situation as there cannot be a limitation to doing justice.

It also rejected the plea alleged verbal consent or lack of objection on the ground that no material was placed on record to substantiate the said plea and held that the State was unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellant had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law, or that it had ever paid any compensation.
It declared that there is no period of limitation prescribed for the courts to exercise their constitutional jurisdiction to do substantial justice.
It directed the State to treat the subject land as a deemed acquisition and disburse compensation to the appellants therein in terms of similar orders passed in other cases within four months.

19. In view of the above settled legal position, we are of the opinion that the stand of the State that it need not pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioner's land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the State is bound to pay Anup Sharma & Ors vs State Of H.P. & Ors on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38275542/
3 market value compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.

sentences.text: Therefore, the writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs.10,000/- and a direction is issued to the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioner utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose and pay him the highest amount towards compensation among compensation under the awards Annexures P-3 and P-4 with all statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act,1894 within eight weeks."

5. In the instant case, the respondents have not established that the subject land owned by the petitioners was voluntarily donated or given by the petitioners willingly for construction of the road in question.p
Land owned by villagers in other villages and utilized for construction of the road has been acquired for in the year 2019.
Petitioners cannot be discriminated.
Their lands utilized for the construction of same road is also to be acquired and compensated for in accordance with law.
In view of above-referred decisions, the relief prayed for by the petitioners cannot be declined to them on the basis of plea of delay and laches.
The respondent, being a welfare State, has to act in just and fair manner after following the due process of law.

In the given facts and circumstances of the case and in light of the legal position, this writ petition is disposed of by directing the respondents to conduct the demarcation of the subject land in accordance with law within a period of four weeks.

On demarcation, in case the land belonging to the petitioners is found to have been utilized for the construction of the road in question, the land acquisition proceedings shall be initiated in respect of such land within a period of eight weeks thereafter.
The same be completed within one year thereafter.

The writ petition stands disposed of in the above terms, so also the pending miscellaneous application(s), if any.
Jyotsna Rewal Dua 1 October, 2024 st Judge (Pardeep)
